## Claim — `domain:ui` execution seat, R19. Unblocked: PR #7169 landed (`5eddeeb68`).

- **Session**: `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7171-scatter-degenerate-sweep`
- **Domain**: `ui` · **Worktree**: dedicated, off `origin/main`
- **Serial constraints cleared**: `plugin-charts` has no other open PR. The three landed answers in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` are all in the tree and verified (`no-positive-flow` 3, `no-positive-magnitude` 1, `unsized-rows` 1, `omitted-rows` 1).

### Clause ② — not engaged

A sweep is a measurement. If it finds a defect, the repair shape is the one #7146 / #7147 / #7148 already landed at normal tier — a refusal or a footnote inside the renderer, no declared surface moved.

### ⚠️ The one thing that must not be inherited

This card exists because scatter's result in #7147's sweep was **NOT MEASURED**, and NOT MEASURED is neither red nor green. Its all-positive control drew **zero marks** (`markN: 0` on *every* scatter tile, the control included), so a control that returns zero is no control, and none of its zeros carry information.

⭐ And the predicate that fixed the other four families almost certainly **does not transfer**. Pie, funnel and treemap size by *magnitude*, so `Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0` is the right test there. **Scatter plots position** — a negative or zero coordinate is perfectly legitimate data. Mechanically reusing `no-positive-magnitude` on scatter would refuse correct charts. The dispatch order carries that as a fence: the degenerate class for a two-measure positional chart has to be *derived*, not copied.

## ✅ LANDED — PR #7197 squash-merged to `main` (`f08cbd996`)

Verified **by content with live controls**. The strongest available shape here is differential: every previously-landed seam answer is still in the same file, so they discriminate a real landing from a broken probe.

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `no-plottable-points` (the new refusal code) | **1** |
| SUBJECT — `unplotted-points` (the new note) | **7** |
| SUBJECT — new suite `AdvancedChartImpl.degeneratePosition.test.tsx` | **1** |
| CONTROL — `no-positive-flow` (#7146) | **3** — still live |
| CONTROL — `no-positive-magnitude` (#7147) | **2** — still live |
| CONTROL — `unsized-rows` (#7148) | **1** — still live |

⭐ All **five** seam codes now coexist in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`, which is the mutual-exclusivity assertion holding in the tree rather than only in the suite.

## The card's premise was NOT MEASURED, and this closed it the right way

This card existed because #7147's scatter result was neither red nor green: its all-positive control drew **zero marks**, so none of its zeros carried information.

**The control drew** — 3 of 3 marks, 245px of mark area, on a run whose live console positive control also fired. And the first test **asserts** that non-zero mark count rather than observing it, so the sweep cannot silently degrade back into blank tiles.

⭐ Better still, the old zero is now *explained* rather than merely superseded: scatter's `XAxis` and `YAxis` are both `type=number` bound to `xAxisKey` and `series[0].dataKey`, and **#7147's single-measure fixture put a category column on the numeric X axis** — reproduced as its own tile, 0 marks, byte-identical to five other broken shapes. A known artefact beats an unexplained one.

## ⭐ The predicate was DERIVED, and the derivation is proved by what copying would have broken

The fence I set was: ⛔ do not reuse #7147's magnitude predicate. It was not merely respected, it was **measured**:

> #7147's magnitude predicate would have blanked the **all-negative (3 of 3 marks)**, **all-zero (2 of 2)** and **mixed-sign (3 of 3)** tiles — which are **correct charts**.

⇒ Mechanical reuse would have **refused three working charts**, which is worse than the silence being fixed. Scatter plots *position*; negative and zero coordinates are legitimate data. That is why a separate scatter-only positional predicate earns its existence.

## What the sweep found

- rows unplaceable on **both** coordinates render **byte-identically (0.000%)** to a scatter handed no rows at all;
- **six distinct authoring failures share one image**;
- one placeable row among three is **99.75% pixel-identical** to a genuinely one-row scatter.

**14 tiles moved, 19 byte-identical**, and all three landed answers keep firing under their own codes.

⚠️ **Zero-variance, constant-x and constant-y are measured-and-DECLINED** — and my A2.3 guess that the interesting failure would be *axis domain collapse* **did not reproduce as collapse**; the real failure there is an axis that renders no scale at all. Naming what the mechanism actually is, instead of accepting my framing, is what Zone 2 exists for.

## ⭐ #7195 — their own pin caught their overreach

An all-boolean scatter coordinate draws nothing and says nothing, and it was **deliberately left unguarded**: a boolean beside a genuinely numeric row draws every mark (3 of 3), so rejecting booleans would put a false "not drawn" count over **visible points**. And the discovery route is the part worth keeping:

> **the first draft DID reject them and the pin went red, which is how the mixed reading was found.**

That is the ablation discipline running *forward*, as a design instrument rather than an after-the-fact proof, and it prevented shipping a refusal that lies about what is on screen.

## Filed, not ridden

**#7194** — graded **p1 `bug`** this round. A multi-series scatter draws every series at the **first** series' y values: two series produced 4 symbols at 2 distinct positions, each drawn twice, with one series' values appearing **nowhere**. ⚠️ Unlike everything this card fixed, that needs **no degenerate input** — valid data, confidently wrong picture, and invisible to inspection because 4 symbols at 2 positions look exactly like legitimate coincident points. It needs a shape ruling and is escalated on #5560.

Clearing `pm:dispatched`.
